metadata.description: An explicit edge to firebase-server:build-base, NOT `^build`. This entry point cannot compile before the parent's dist exists, so the edge is real -- but it has to be spelled out, because `^build` here would resolve to firebase-server:build, which depends on this very target: a hard cycle. That XOR is the whole design constraint -- either the children get `^build` or the parent aggregates them, never both. Aggregating is the side that keeps one writer per dist directory.  This entry point also imports @dereekb/firebase-server/model, a SIBLING entry point in this same family, so it carries an in-family edge to `firebase-server-model:build-base`. A sibling edge is spelled as `build-base` (not `build`): siblings compile into this same dist directory and have no `build` of their own, and the parent's `build` is what depends on all of them, so pointing at it here would close the cycle the parent-edge comment describes. It further imports @dereekb/zoho/nestjs, another family's CHILD, hence `zoho:build`. Cross-family deps are spelled as the other family's ROOT `build` (not `build-base`, and not that family's child project): a sibling family's child has no `build` of its own and writes into its parent's dist, so the parent's `build` -- which runs the ESM finalize -- is the only thing that produces a finalized copy for TypeScript to resolve `exports` against.
